name: EWA Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's top belt of 2003 and 2004. Camaro won its title tournament at Kingdom Come on 10 May 2003 and its page counts ten reigns to Brett Cotter on 27 November 2004. The page's sixth row carries a note that the WWO Championship and the EWA Championship were unified into the EWA Undisputed Heavyweight Championship on 27 March 2004, under a reign dated 17 January 2004; the Sinners card of May 2004 bills the title as the EWA Undisputed World Heavyweight Championship.

name: EWA European Championship
epitaph: A mid-card belt held from its first reign on 5 April 2003 (Dragon) through twenty reigns to Crucifix on 30 April 2005. Its page footnotes two events: Richard Bison was stripped on 9 September 2003 for injuring a rival to keep him out of an Elimination Chamber, and the title was unified with the WWO Internet Championship at Collision 2004 under David Boyce's reign.

name: EWA Survival Championship
epitaph: A belt whose first champion, Joker, is dated 5 April 2003, the same day as the European Championship's. Its page lists sixteen reigns to Mark Fletcher on 25 September 2004, including a vacancy before Sense Green's win on 26 June 2004.

name: EWA Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The tag belts, with fourteen reigns on its page from a survivor match at the TTTTT2 on 5 July 2003 to Brett Cotter and Michael Bendis, The Regulators, on 14 September 2004. The page numbers two different reigns 6; its date for the last reign sits ten days after the news of 4 September 2004 reports The Regulators winning the titles from Gekido.

name: EWA Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: A short lineage of three reigns in 2004: Michael Bendis won it in a Battle Royal at Wipe Out on 26 June 2004, Rage took it in a Ladder Match on 4 August and Joker on 21 August. Mark Fletcher's biography says the Cruiserweight Title was the earlier Rising Star Title renamed.

name: EWA TV Championship
epitaph: Five reigns in 2004, from a unification of the EWA Rising Star Championship and the WWO TV Championship on 21 February 2004 (Keith, beating Alexander) to Lotus, who won a five-way on Sinners 2 on 23 May 2004. Four of the five champions appear on the page only as pictures and are named from the pictures' file names; the next row's beaten champion, or the Sinners 2 card, bears out each name.

name: EWA Legacy Championship
epitaph: The main-event title of the fed's 2008 pages, whose rules call it the most prestigious title in the EWA. Its champions page lists thirteen reigns, from Scott Acid (Sinners IV) to Richard Bison, who won it on 24 December 2007 (Monday Night Shockers) and is the champion at the page's end. Only the shows are given for most changes; the page dates two.

name: EWA Internet Championship
epitaph: The fed's second belt in its 2008 rules, an upper and mid-card title. Its champions page lists fourteen reigns from 'Shockers Jan 30th' to Matt Wolfe, who won it on 7 January 2008 (Monday Night Shockers). The page does not give the years of its earlier changes.

name: EWA Breakthrough Championship
epitaph: The lower-card belt of the 2008 pages. Its champions page gives eighteen reigns in two lists that meet at Dominic Deaver, champion from Shockers December 25th: the past list runs from Scott Acid (Collision 2006) and ends his reign at Ground Zero, where the Calamity list also ends; the current list, under a note that the two titles have been unified, carries him on to Ascension and runs to Daigo Prisken (Ground Zero III).

name: EWA Calamity Championship
epitaph: A belt the 2008 champions page lists only as past: eight Calamity champions from Treize Delacroix (Shockers Jan 30th) to Chris Kane (Wipe Out to Ground Zero), after which its page says the Calamity and Breakthrough Championships were unified.
